transcript.content: Hello. What brings you to the clinic today?
I can’t stop obsessing over how terrible I look in photos and at events, and it’s making me want to avoid people altogether. It has just gotten so overwhelming lately, and I don't know what to do.

Do you worry because you believe there is a specific flaw or defect in your physical appearance that others will notice, or is your main fear that you will act embarrassingly or be judged by others in social situations?

It is definitely about specific flaws in my appearance. I am completely obsessed with how saggy and crooked my face, jawline, and neck look, and I am convinced everyone else is noticing it too. It's not about how I act; I'm just deeply embarrassed by how I look, even though my family says they don't see what I'm talking about.
How long have you been experiencing these intense worries about your face, jawline, and neck?

It has been going on for several months now. It all started after a milestone birthday party a few months ago where they showed a slideshow of candid photos of me. Ever since then, I haven't been able to stop obsessing over my sagging jawline, neck, and all these wrinkles.
Do you find yourself frequently checking your face in mirrors, trying to hide or camouflage your jawline and neck, or asking others for reassurance about how you look?

Yes, I do, and it's honestly so embarrassing. I spend hours standing inches from the mirror tilting my head, changing my hair or glasses to hide my neck, and taking selfies just to zoom in on my wrinkles. I also constantly corner my husband and sister, begging them to tell me if my face looks lopsided or awful.
On average, how much time do you spend each day on these thoughts and behaviors, and has it interfered with your ability to work or go about your daily routine?

I easily spend several hours every single day trapped in these thoughts and checking myself. It has completely taken over my life, forcing me to skip choir practice, turn down my theater volunteering, and even consider canceling my retirement party. I'm just too ashamed to have anyone look at me right now.
Have you consulted with any dermatologists or plastic surgeons, or have you considered getting cosmetic procedures to try to fix these areas of your face and neck?

No, I haven't consulted with any dermatologists or plastic surgeons, and I haven't sought out any cosmetic procedures. When I broke down and explained how I was feeling during a routine visit, my primary care doctor referred me directly here for psychiatric care instead.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all diagnostic criteria for Body Dysmorphic Disorder (ICD-10: F45.22). She exhibits a severe preoccupation with perceived physical defects in her face, jawline, neck, and wrinkles that are not observable or appear only slight to others (her family does not see them). This preoccupation leads to significant repetitive behaviors, including excessive mirror checking, camouflaging with hair/glasses, taking and zooming in on selfies, and reassurance seeking. The symptoms cause marked functional impairment, leading her to avoid social activities like choir practice and volunteering, and have persisted for several months.
